Synthetic Data for Table 1 Examples

example_table1_data.Rd

Returns fixed synthetic observations with continuous, factor, character, and numeric-coded categorical covariates, missing values, three groups (Control, Treatment, Registry), nonconstant analysis weights, and survey-design identifiers. The function takes no arguments and does not alter the random-number generator state, so results are identical on every call.

Usage

example_table1_data()

Value

A data.frame with 90 rows and the columns group (factor), age, bmi (continuous, with missing values), sex (factor, with missing values), smoking (character, with missing values), stage_code (numeric codes 1 to 3, with missing values), analysis_weight (positive weights), stratum (North/South, no missing values), and cluster (unique identifier per row).

Examples

d <- example_table1_data()
head(d)
#>     group age  bmi    sex smoking stage_code analysis_weight stratum cluster
#> 1 Control  43 20.3 Female   Never          1             1.6   North       1
#> 2 Control  50 21.6   Male    <NA>          1             2.7   South       2
#> 3 Control  57 22.9   <NA> Current          2             3.8   North       3
#> 4 Control  NA 24.2   Male   Never          3             4.9   South       4
#> 5 Control  71 25.5 Female  Former         NA             6.0   North       5
#> 6 Control  78 26.8 Female   Never          3             7.1   South       6
table(d$group)
#> 
#>   Control Treatment  Registry 
#>        30        30        30 
colSums(is.na(d))   # which columns contain missing values
#>           group             age             bmi             sex         smoking 
#>               0               3               4               3               3 
#>      stage_code analysis_weight         stratum         cluster 
#>               3               0               0               0
